rationale: Australian online home retailer with brand-building ambitions at home; Melbourne Grand Prix is local, but F1 fit is limited.

name: Brightline
desc: Virtual mental health provider offering therapy, coaching and psychiatry for children, teens and families through video sessions.
markets: Families in the United States, covered by insurance and employer plans.
rationale: US virtual care provider with a sensitive health audience and no international footprint; F1 fit is weak.

name: Hayat Holding
desc: Turkish group whose subsidiaries make Molfix and Bebem diapers, Papia tissue, Bingo detergents and Kastamonu Entegre wood panels.
markets: Consumer brands sold in Turkey, the Middle East, Europe, Russia and Central Asia.
rationale: Marketing-led consumer brands with regional growth; Turkish and Middle East GP exposure is plausible but unconfirmed.

name: Traeger
desc: Maker of wood pellet grills and smokers, with pellets, rubs, sauces, accessories and a connected cooking app.
markets: Consumers in the United States, Canada, Europe and Australia through retailers and online.
rationale: Lifestyle brand with an enthusiast audience and American Grands Prix hospitality fit, but its finances are limited.

name: Haohaizi
desc: Chinese baby care products maker and retailer selling infant clothing and care items through shops and online.
markets: Customers in China only; current ownership and status not confirmed.
rationale: Little-known Chinese baby products brand with unconfirmed current status; no F1 case.

name: SPORT 2000
desc: French cooperative network of franchised and independent stores selling sportswear, footwear and equipment.
markets: Shoppers in France through hundreds of independent and franchised stores.
rationale: Cooperative retail network with a domestic base and no central marketing budget; limited F1 relevance.

name: Aukey
desc: Shenzhen-based consumer electronics brand selling chargers, power banks, cables, car accessories and small gadgets, mostly through Amazon.
markets: Sold through online marketplaces to consumers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Online-led accessories brand with international customers; tech tie-in is plausible but a marketplace model limits spend.

name: PFS
desc: Irving, Texas business that Crunchbase tags as business-to-business consumer goods; what it sells is not confirmed.
markets: Products, customers and markets not confirmed; no verified international activity.
rationale: Unidentified company with an ambiguous name; no basis for an F1 rationale.

name: Ultrajaya
desc: Indonesian dairy and beverage maker known for Ultra Milk UHT milk, Teh Kotak boxed tea and Buavita juice.
markets: Consumers across Indonesia through supermarkets, minimarkets and traditional retail.
rationale: Mass-market Indonesian beverage brands with strong local marketing; F1 is a stretch without international ambitions.

name: Baozun
desc: E-commerce services company running online stores in China for global and local brands, including marketing, service and fulfilment.
markets: Brand clients and consumers in mainland China only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: B2B e-commerce service provider tied to China; some brand-client hospitality value but weak F1 fit.

name: WageWorks
desc: Administrator of pre-tax employee benefit accounts such as flexible spending, health savings and commuter benefits for employers.
markets: Employers and employees in the United States only; no international operations or plans.
rationale: US benefits administrator folded into another provider; no consumer marketing case for F1.

name: Lifestyle Communities
desc: Developer and operator of manufactured home communities for over-50s in Victoria where residents own homes and rent land.
markets: Residents in Victoria, Australia only; no international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Local property developer for over-50s with no international footprint; F1 fit is weak.

name: Hero K12
desc: Education software company building student behaviour management tools, such as attendance and tardy tracking, sold to US schools.
markets: Schools and districts in the United States only; no verified international activity.
rationale: Niche school software sold to districts with no consumer marketing need; F1 fit is weak.

name: Meituan
desc: Chinese local services platform covering food delivery, restaurant reviews, travel booking, instant retail and group buying, with Keeta abroad.
markets: Consumers in China, with Keeta food delivery in Hong Kong, the Middle East and Brazil.
rationale: Consumer platform expanding Keeta in the Gulf and Latin America where F1 audiences are strong; plausible brand-awareness play.

name: Rakuten
desc: Japanese internet group running the Rakuten Ichiba marketplace, card and bank, mobile network, travel, Viber and Kobo businesses.
markets: Consumers and merchants mainly in Japan, plus Viber, Kobo and advertising operations across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Global brand already linked to Ferrari from 2027, so a direct F1 tie-in exists.
f1: Named on the roster as a Ferrari partner from 2027.

name: Amplifon
desc: Hearing care retailer running thousands of shops under Amplifon, Miracle-Ear and other brands, offering audiology services and hearing aids.
markets: Shops in about 26 countries across Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.
rationale: International consumer health retailer with brand-building needs, though older audience limits F1 fit; hospitality value is moderate.

name: goeasy
desc: Canadian non-prime consumer lender and lease provider operating easyfinancial loans, easyhome lease-to-own and LendCare point-of-sale financing.
markets: Customers in Canada only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Canadian non-prime lender with a domestic base and regulatory sensitivity around consumer credit; weak F1 fit.

name: PayPal
desc: Digital payments company running the PayPal wallet, Venmo, Braintree, Xoom and Honey, earning transaction fees from merchants and consumers.
markets: Merchants and consumers in more than 200 markets across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Global payments brand with merchant and consumer audiences, strong for brand exposure and B2B hospitality; no current roster link.

name: Consumer Cellular
desc: US mobile virtual network operator selling wireless plans and phones mainly to people over 50, via retail, AARP and online.
markets: Customers in the United States only, on AT&T and T-Mobile networks.
rationale: US-only carrier aimed at older customers, so F1's audience mismatch and domestic scope make fit weak.

name: Allegro
desc: Poland's largest e-commerce marketplace, also running Ceneo, the Mall group, Allegro Pay and the Allegro Smart delivery service.
markets: Shoppers in Poland and Central Europe including the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia and Croatia.
rationale: Dominant Central European marketplace seeking brand reach; F1 offers regional exposure and hospitality, but no known interest.

name: Klarna
desc: Swedish fintech offering buy now pay later, instalments, a shopping app, debit card and savings account to shoppers and merchants.
markets: Shoppers and merchants across Europe, the United States and Australia.
rationale: Brand-led consumer fintech with Europe and US reach and a young audience; F1 offers visibility and merchant hospitality.

name: Mercado Libre
desc: Latin American e-commerce and fintech platform running the Mercado Libre marketplace, Mercado Pago payments, logistics and credit.
markets: Consumers and merchants in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and other Latin American countries.
rationale: Latin America's largest online platform with Mexico and Brazil Grand Prix exposure; already named on the F1 partner list.

name: Belk
desc: US department store chain with more than 250 stores in the Southeast selling apparel, shoes, cosmetics and home goods.
markets: Shoppers in the southeastern United States only; no international operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Regional US department store with limited brand-marketing budget and no international footprint; weak F1 fit.
